simple: Services are Roblox's built-in toolkits, like `Players` for player info, `TweenService` for smooth animations, and `DataStoreService` for saving data. You get them with `game:GetService("Name")`. Almost every script follows the same pattern: get services, require modules, write functions, and connect them to events. Learning which service does what is a big part of making games.
analogy: Services are like departments in a big company: if you need something paid, you go to Finance; if you need a delivery, you go to Shipping. In Roblox, you ask the right service for the job.
keyPoints: Get a service with `game:GetService("ServiceName")`, and store it in a variable with the same name, like `local Players = game:GetService("Players")`.
The common script pattern is: 1) get services, 2) require modules, 3) write local functions, 4) connect events that call those functions.
Use `WaitForChild` when finding things, because Roblox does not promise what loads first.
Container services hold objects: `Workspace` (the 3D world), `Lighting` (sky and light effects), `ReplicatedStorage` and `ReplicatedFirst` (shared between server and clients).
Scripting services add features: `TweenService` (smooth changes), `MarketplaceService` (purchases), `RunService` (every-frame updates), `SoundService` (audio), `CollectionService` (tags).
Cloud services work over the internet: `DataStoreService` (saving data between visits), `MemoryStoreService` (fast short-term data), `MessagingService` (talking between servers).

terms.service: A built-in Roblox object that gives you a group of related features.
terms.game: A global variable that points to the very top of your game's data model.
terms.data model: The whole tree of everything in your game, as shown in the Explorer.
terms.container service: A service that holds other objects, like Workspace holding all your parts.
terms.cloud service: A service that runs on Roblox's internet servers, so data can last after players leave.
terms.persistent data: Data that is saved and still there next time, like a player's coins.
terms.ephemeral data: Short-lived data that changes quickly and does not need to be kept forever, like a live matchmaking queue.
terms.tween: A smooth change from one value to another over time, like a door sliding open over 1 second.
terms.convention: A common habit everyone follows so code is easy to read, like naming the variable `Players` for the Players service.

example.title: Greet players and count them
example.code:
-- 1. Get services
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- 2. (Require modules would go here)

-- 3. Local functions
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
	print(player.Name .. " joined! Players online: " .. #Players:GetPlayers())
end

local function onPlayerRemoving(player)
	print(player.Name .. " left.")
end

-- 4. Connect events to the functions
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(onPlayerRemoving)
explain: We get the `Players` service once, at the top, and name the variable after it.
We write two small local functions for joining and leaving.
`#Players:GetPlayers()` counts how many players are in the server.
Finally we connect the functions to the `PlayerAdded` and `PlayerRemoving` events, so they run at the right time.

watchOut: Use `game:GetService("Players")` instead of `game.Players`. `GetService` is the reliable way to get services.
Service names must be spelled exactly, with the right capital letters.
Do not call `GetService` over and over inside loops. Get it once at the top of the script.
Cloud services like `DataStoreService` can fail when the internet has trouble. Wrap their calls in `pcall`.
